title: Bears to honor Mike Ditka by wearing this helmet decal in Week 5 against Packers - CBS Sports
description: Ditka, who played six years in Chicago before leading the Bears to a Super Bowl as a coach, passed away last week
body:
Ditka, who played six years in Chicago before leading the Bears to a Super Bowl as a coach, passed away last week.
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:17 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Mike Ditka is one of the most legendary figures in Chicago Bears history, and the team is planning to honor him on Sunday. For their Week 5 game in Green Bay, the Bears will be wearing a special helmet decal that will feature Ditka's 89, which was the number he wore during his six-year career as a player in Chicago. The Bears unveiled the decal on Sunday morning. 
Ditka died Friday at the age of 86. Ditka is an icon in Chicago, and his ties with the franchise go back 65 years. In 1961, the Bears made him the fifth overall pick in the NFL Draft. During his rookie season, he became the first tight end in NFL history to go over 1,000 yards receiving. He ended up spending a total of 12 seasons in the NFL, with six of those coming in Chicago. He also played for the Eagles (1967-68) and Cowboys (1969-72). 
After his playing career ended, Ditka returned to Chicago when the Bears hired him as head coach in 1982. Three years later, he led the Bears to their first, and currently only, Super Bowl win in franchise history. Ditka ended up coaching the Bears for 11 seasons (1982-1992), and he was voted the NFL's coach of the year twice (1985, 1988) during that span. Ditka is such an NFL legend that the Packers will also be honoring the Pro Football Hall of Famer on Sunday. According to the Chicago Sun-Times, the team is planning a moment of silence before the game. "One of the fiercest competitors in NFL history, Mike helped define the intensity and tradition of the Packers-Bears rivalry, the oldest in professional football," the Packers said in a statement. "He embodied the toughness and passion that have made the rivalry one of the most storied in all of sports. While he was a formidable opponent, his contributions to the game and to a rivalry that has meant so much to both franchises will always be respected and remembered by the Green Bay Packers."
The Bears and Packers will be kicking off at 1 p.m. ET from Lambeau Field.

title: Alabama QB Keelon Russell wins Georgia over with postgame gesture - CBS Sports
description: The 19-year-old quarterback shrugged off his first career loss to show respect to Stockton, earning high praise f
body:
The 19-year-old quarterback shrugged off his first career loss to show respect to Stockton, earning high praise from Georgia coach Kirby Smart along the way
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:12 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        TUSCALOOSA, Ala. -- Minutes after losing to No. 2 Georgia, Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell quietly stood and waited. His teammates had already headed to the locker room after the 20-17 loss to the Bulldogs inside Bryant-Denny Stadium. Some looked mad, some looked shell-shocked. It was a mix of sprinting off as quickly as possible and slowly meandering toward the locker room. And then there was Russell, the first-year Alabama starting quarterback who has been a revelation for the Crimson Tide. He had just suffered his first loss as a starter, the kind of game that gnaws at you knowing that if a play or two (or controversial call) goes the other way, the result would have been different. It wasn't Russell's best game, either, though he did enough to give his team more than a chance to walk away with a win. He stood and waited as Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton got the victorious star treatment in an ESPN on-field interview. He stood and waited as the interview seemed to drag on for minutes, as an Alabama staffer tried in vain to corral him to the locker room. He waited all to congratulate Stockton on his performance in the Bulldogs' win. 
"Win or lose, I have respect for the opponent no matter what," Russell said. "Gunner Stockton is an amazing player. Guy's a baller. I have respect for everybody that we play, so I wanted to give my dues to him that you're a great player."
The most amazing thing? There wasn't a preexisting relationship before Saturday night. It wasn't Russell waiting to congratulate one of his best friends. Stockton said after the game they had never even talked before that postgame moment, though he was obviously well aware of Russell's skills. The genuine moment from the 19-year-old rising star in Tuscaloosa impressed the 22-year old veteran quarterback who just had to go toe-to-toe with him for hours inside Bryant-Denny Stadium. 
"He was awesome," Stockton said. "I've tried to do better with that, trying to go shake the other quarterback's hand no matter what. Seeing that at a younger age is pretty, pretty special."With a maturity that already belies his youth, the sky is the limit for Russell at Alabama. And it would be no surprise at all to see Russell guiding the Crimson Tide to a rematch against the Bulldogs, whether in the SEC Championship or the College Football Playoff."There is no containing Russell," Georgia coach Kirby Smart said. "Kid's an elite athlete, an elite player. Hopefully we affected him some tonight and he didn't have some of the numbers he's had, but he's a really good football player. He's going to be hell in this league for two years."

title: Mourinho skips press conference after Vini Jr.'s hair-pulling incident - CBS Sports
description: The Portuguese coach was reportedly furious after the game against Villarreal and decided to not talk with the me
body:
The Portuguese coach was reportedly furious after the game against Villarreal and decided to not talk with the media
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:00 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho didn't speak to the media after the game against Villarreal on Saturday as he wanted to "avoid a possible suspension," according to multiple reports. Mourinho, known for his character on and off the pitch, was furious in the second half after VAR decided to call the referee to the monitor and call off the goal scored by Brazilian striker Vinicius Jr., who was also sent off by the referee as VAR review showed he had pulled Nathan Saliba's hair before scoring. Mourinho, who rejoined Real Madrid as coach in the summer, didn't take part in the media activities and didn't attend the usual post-match press conference at the Bernabeu, following Real Madrid's 1-0 win against Villarreal thanks to the goal of Yan Diomande.After the game, Vinicius Jr. apologized to fans and his teammates as he posted on Instagram."Sorry to the team and the fans," he said.
The Brazilian striker came on in the 52nd minute and was sent off 20 minutes later. Mourinho celebrated alongside his team and ran over to Vinicius Jr. a few seconds before VAR overturned the decision and sent him off. The Spanish Football Federation rules state that pulling the opponent's hair is considered violent conduct and the sanction (Article 130) is a ban of one to three games. Real Madrid will face Sevilla, Barcelona and Racing Santander, meaning that it is likely that Vinicius Jr. will miss the Clasico against Barcelona on Oct. 25. Mourinho will be back speaking on Tuesday when Real Madrid will travel to Rome ahead of the second Champions League match of the league phase that will take place on Wednesday at the Stadio Olimpico against AS Roma, live on Paramount+. It will also be the first comeback of the Special One at the Olimpico since he was sacked by the Giallorossi in January 2024. 
Mourinho left a lasting legacy at the club he managed from 2021 to 2024, guiding them to their first-ever UEFA trophy by winning the inaugural UEFA Conference League in 2022. He later led the team to the 2023 UEFA Europa League final, where they suffered a penalty shootout defeat to Sevilla. His emotional return to face his former club is set to be one of the most anticipated moments of this Champions League season.

title: USWNT's errors stick out almost as much as their strengths in loss to Spain - CBS Sports
description: Spain scored twice in the opening minutes thanks to Patri Guijarro and Eva Navarro, creating a hole the USWNT cou
body:
Spain scored twice in the opening minutes thanks to Patri Guijarro and Eva Navarro, creating a hole the USWNT could not dig themselves out of
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:31 am ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        WASHINGTON, D.C. -- Crystal Dunn may no longer be a member of the U.S. women's national team, but a Women's World Cup winner's finger is not necessarily far from the pulse, even in retirement. Shortly before the reigning Olympic champions faced the reigning world champions in a friendly, she outlined the theme of the week succinctly."I don't want us to win easy."The simple logic is that there are no shortcuts to the top, especially in a women's soccer landscape that is more competitive with each passing day. The USWNT did not get the easy win they were trying to avoid on Saturday after all; instead, they came away with a complex 2-0 loss to Spain that saw their shortcomings share the same pitch as their defining qualities. The U.S. team were uneven and imperfect, unsurprising considering they faced a foe who was always going to pose questions and did as soon as the opening whistle blew. Eight months before a World Cup, though, questions are not such a bad thing."I don't think it's always necessarily a bad thing to lose," Trinity Rodman said post-match.Emma Hayes' side grew into the game, so much so that they ultimately outshot Spain 13 to six and racked up 2.26 expected goals to Spain's 0.43. The visitors' attack was limited to zero shots in the second half, a signal that the USWNT's game plan had its merits. They were ultimately outdone by a rough start – Patri Guijarro and Eva Navarro scored within the opening 14 minutes, the U.S. team's defensive operation exposed in different ways despite the impressive finishes from Spain's goalscorers.
"One, it's a great strike but really we've got to do better than that," Hayes said. "Second goal, their goalkeeper's got the ball and we've got numbers behind the ball but we don't do our job well enough as a collective."
Those first 15 minutes were unforgiving to the USWNT's defenders and midfielders, even if the second half was redeeming. Hayes went with Tierna Davidson and Kennedy Wesley at center back, the pair playing together for the first time, though the head coach had little choice – Naomi Girma was ruled out of the friendlies against Spain with an injury. The highlight reel on Navarro's goal will be unkind to Wesley but she was far from the only one, a U.S. midfield featuring Lindsey Heaps, Lily Yohannes and Rose Lavelle unable to do their best on both Spain strikes. There were as many individual failings as collective ones, Hayes argued."If you're defending and you jump out in the wrong moment and then the back line drops, well, the midfielder, whoever you are, is always going to be exposed because there's too much distance in front and there's too much distance in behind," Hayes said. "I didn't think we got that right as a collective in the first half and so we have to position any midfielder to be in a better place to be able to manage the quality of their players when they play close together. You can't have big gaps, but when you're 2-0 down, that maybe it creates a little bit of doubt in your head around drop-off and those things, so I don't think we helped our midfield as a collective approach. I think it's a team game. I don't think it's about one unit. I think it's about the whole and I think that whoever was on the field grew into the game, and I said, [we] didn't finish."
Navarro's goal threatened to suck the energy out of the USWNT, to the point that the team gathered right after before resuming play.
"We have to keep going," Yohannes said of the discussion. "It's early. We have a lot of time and then just little tactical things that someone saw something. We just said it and keep the communication, positive energy."Tactical shifts at halftime helped, including Lavelle taking more of a wide role on the right, restoring some balance after their forward play veered heavily to the left during the first. They also allowed the U.S. team to do exactly what it set out to do, their shot creation encouraging enough despite an inability to score that Hayes described as a consistent problem. In a test of the USWNT's depth and the team's range of options, not every concern was assuaged. Heaps is not well-suited to play as the deepest midfielder on the pitch against a team of Spain's caliber, Hayes making a fascinating choice there despite having Claire Hutton as an option even if Sam Coffey was unavailable through injury. Heaps' attack-minded tendencies remain her strong suit but the USWNT's midfield can still look unresolved at times, a problem Hayes inherited but has yet to find the perfect solution for.
Even if the USWNT improved in the second half, it was hard not to notice that the midfield was failing to accomplish its objectives, even if they were far from the only ones."I think me and Lindsay were sort of [in] a pivot role together, trying to stay close to each other when they're pressing high, providing options to our back line, getting second balls, winning our duels," Yohannes said. "That's our role and that's what we tried to do. I think it was spells of good moments when we, I think, were winning a lot of duels and going into sort of transitions with them but like I said, when we tried to kind of fall back, they were good at playing against low blocks and when we're not able to get pressure on the ball, it's tough."Heaps concurred."The two goals wasn't directly off of them playing through us or breaking us down," Heaps noted. "I mean, they had quality in their finishes but it was almost due to our lack of not stepping to the ball or maybe us giving them a transition moment and obviously a back post cross that maybe we can prevent … Defensively, we got to stay compact and keep the lines tight but be able to get enough pressure on them and especially don't let them play through us too quickly."
The USWNT's pre-World Cup qualification schedule has almost been building up to this moment, though. Friendlies against Japan in April and Brazil in June continue to afford them the experiences of a potential knockout match next summer, ones that come down to fine margins and moments that can come and go in a flash."When you play the best team in the world, you have to execute everything really well in the first instance," Hayes said. "You can't afford to go 2-0 down against the best team in the world, especially the way we conceded those goals but that's the learning and did I think we did enough to score a goal? Of course we did. Did we ever do enough to score more than one? Absolutely. We just didn't make, necessarily, the right decisions and execute with the quality I know us to [have] but I think a lot of things are really good about what we did but not those."

title: Oregon gets an 'A' mark while Texas earns 'C-' on Week 8 report card - CBS Sports
description: A look at how national championship contenders fared in Week 6 action
body:
A look at how national championship contenders fared in Week 6 action
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:01 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        It's a good thing Oregon coach Dan Lanning has four straight seasons of 10+ victories in his back pocket, because otherwise the Ducks coach might be feeling a little warmth under his seat after the way his team played Saturday. Oregon committed seven turnovers in a 17-15 loss to a UCLA team led by first-year coach Bob Chesney.Ducks quarterback Dylan Raiola looked unprepared and poorly coached, and Lanning waited far too long to pull him. Additionally, Lanning's peculiar decision to go for two after a touchdown in the first quarter came back to haunt Oregon late in the fourth quarter.Oregon's 3-2 start includes two losses as a double-digit favorite against teams under first-year coaches. At this point, it seems clear how reliant Lanning was on offensive coordinator Will Stein, who is in the midst of leading Kentucky to a 5-1 start. Lanning looks lost, the offense looks horrible and the Ducks are sliding into the abyss. The only possible redemption for Oregon would be running the table and defeating Ohio State on Nov. 7 on the road. It's hard to imagine that after what we've seen from this team through five games.
        
            
                Tom Fornelli's CFP Vibe Check: Did the Big 12 outsmart everybody?
                
                    Tom Fornelli                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
We are handing out grades evaluating every team that started or ended the day with national championship odds of +3000 or better. No. 4 Miami (+750) was off this week.
Teams listed in order of their AP Top 25 ranking. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 1 TexasGrade: D  Result: 27-24 loss vs. Oklahoma  Title odds: +850Texas quarterback Arch Manning suffered a meltdown in the fourth quarter, throwing a pick-six that let Oklahoma take the lead. Then, his second interception in the final minute helped Oklahoma get in position for a game-winning field goal. The Sooners also scored on a blocked punt as two of their three touchdowns were of the non-offensive variety. Gifting scores to the Sooners was the only way Texas could lose against such an offensively lifeless opponent. Texas let it happen. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 2 GeorgiaGrade: B+  Result: 20-17 win at Alabama  Title odds: +490While it's true that Georgia benefitted from favorable officiating and a couple of lucky bounces, the Bulldogs also showed championship-level traits while earning a season-defining road win. Georgia averaged an impressive 7.5 yards per play and repeatedly came up with defensive answers in key situations. Every Alabama series ended either at midfield or in UGA territory, but only two of them ended in touchdowns as the Bulldogs kept the Crimson Tide under constant pressure.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 3 Notre DameGrade: A  Result: 58-7 win vs. Stanford  Title odds: +470Notre Dame's breezed through its final tune-up before a top-10 clash with BYU as the Fighting Irish jumped out to a 37-0 halftime lead against a hapless Stanford team. The running game continued making strides, highlighted by freshman Jonaz Walton's 97-yard touchdown run in the second quarter. The Cardinal only got past their own 35-yard line once in their first nine possessions amidst another dominant showing from the Fighting Irish defense. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 5 Ohio StateGrade: C+  Result: 45-16 win vs. Maryland  Title odds: +370Ohio State was never in any real danger against a bad Maryland team, but the Buckeyes didn't play a clean game on a rain-soaked day at Ohio Stadium. They turned it over twice, leading to 10 Maryland points and committed eight penalties. With Indiana up next and the Buckeyes resting a few starters, the assignment was essentially to survive and advance without significant drama or major health issues. From that standpoint, the Buckeyes passed.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 6 AlabamaGrade: B-  Result: 20-17 loss vs. Georgia  Title odds: +950Facing a great defense for the first time all season, Alabama struggled to execute in some key situations. The Crimson Tide lined up to go for it on a fourth-and-4 from Georgia's 43 with the game tied early in the fourth quarter and were called for a false start, which forced them to punt. Then, Alabama gave up a third-down sack to fall out of field goal range on its next series, which turned out to be its last. A first quarter fumble that ended a promising series in UGA territory also loomed large over a game that Bama feels like it should have won.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 7 IndianaGrade: B  Result: 20-17 win at Nebraska  Title odds: +1000Indiana played a C- level game until the final 12 minutes, when it flipped a switch and roared back from a 17-6 deficit. With its running game bottled up, IU needed its passing game to provide the punch. It did, as Nick Marsh scored on touchdown grabs of 75 and 44 yards from Josh Hoover during the comeback. The Hoosiers had some problems containing Nebraska quarterback Anthony Colandrea, but they stiffened up late and didn't allow the Cornhuskers into IU territory on their final four possessions. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 9 Ole MissGrade: A-  Result: 52-17 win at Vanderbilt  Title odds: +2700The competitive portion of this game ended in the second quarter as Ole Miss raced out to a 42-3 halftime lead en route to a rare easy win in the SEC. Two of the Rebels' touchdowns came in the final minute of the first half courtesy of Vanderbilt fumbles as the Commodores struggled to get out of their own way. Still, Ole Miss racked up nearly 300 yards of offense in the first half and scored touchdowns on four straight possessions while looking sharp after a bye week.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 10 LSUGrade: C-Result: 35-34 (OT) loss at KentuckyTitle odds: +2700Kentucky missed two field goals with under five minutes remaining and LSU leading 27-24. It was almost as if the Wildcats were inviting the Tigers to win. But Lane Kiffin's offense couldn't sustain a drive either time. Stunningly, Kiffin elected not to go for it on fourth-and-1 from his own 43-yard line with 1:46 remaining. A first down would have ended the game. Instead, he punted, and the Tigers allowed Kentucky to drive for the game-tying field goal before losing in overtime. Kiffin's unusual conservatism cost his team in a game they could ill-afford to lose. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 13 OregonGrade: FResult: 17-15 loss vs. UCLATitle odds: +7000Oregon turned in a deplorable effort against UCLA and would have been blown out had the Bruins not missed numerous opportunities to build their lead. The Ducks finally pulled ineffective quarterback Dylan Raiola in the fourth quarter, and third-string QB Brock Thomas led a rally. But this game was lost over the first three quarters in a sea of turnovers, offensive ineptitude and bad coaching decisions.

title: Steve Sarkisian will still call plays, not considering staff changes after Texas' loss to Oklahoma - CBS Sports
description: It's time for the Longhorns' coach to admit his staff isn't performing up to expectations
body:
It's time for the Longhorns' coach to admit his staff isn't performing up to expectations
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:08 am ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Arrogance brings down empires and for Texas coach Steve Sarkisian, his reluctance to make tough, coaching staff adjustments during a season in which all resources have been pushed to the center of the table may come back to haunt the Longhorns.Sarkisian stiff-armed the idea of giving up play-calling duties or shuffling his special teams staff following Saturday's 27-24 loss to Oklahoma, a rivalry matchup that exposed some of his team's season-long flaws."Not a chance," Sarkisian said of stepping away from his dual-role of coach and calling the offense. "We have to play better."Matched up with one of the SEC's worst offenses coming into the Red River Rivalry game, Texas whipped up a recipe that made the setting ripe for an upset after giving up a special teams score in the first half on a punt block and a defensive touchdown later.
It marked the second straight game the Longhorns failed in the kicking game after Tennessee's Qua Moss scored on a 57-yard punt return in Knoxville.
        
            
                College football bowl projections: Slotting all 46 games, new CFP teams after Oklahoma, UCLA upsets
                
                    Brad Crawford                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Sarkisian quickly fired "no" to a question about "reevaluating Jeff Banks' responsibilities on special teams" in the aftermath, backing an assistant coach who has failed to deliver in big spots recently.During last season's loss at Georgia, the Longhorns were fooled by a successful onside kick and through five games, Texas ranks in the bottom-half of the SEC this season in kickoff and punting average, kickoff return average and is one of eight SEC teams without a blocked punt or kick yet.
"I feel like we've missed some opportunities on special teams quite frankly," Sarkisian said. "I felt like we had a couple return opportunities that we didn't get. Clearly, two weeks in a row we've kicked the ball out of bounds on kickoffs. We're better than that, and so I've got to find a way to get our guys playing with more confidence from a specialist standpoint. But again, that's my job to try to get that done."Offensive struggles persist at TexasSarkisian has shouldered much of the special teams blame, but hasn't looked in the mirror yet to determine why the Longhorns are battling offensive deficiencies — despite one of the most-talented personnel groupings nationally on his side of the football.Texas went three-and-out seven times against Oklahoma and currently leads the SEC in three-and-out rate this season, averaging just 1.63 points per possession in two conference matchups (which ranks 103rd in college football).
The Longhorns' 5.4 yards per play average coming out of Saturday's loss this season ranks 104th nationally, only ahead of Power Four offensive doormats like Arkansas, Clemson, Texas A&M, Michigan and Colorado.Arch Manning's pick-six in the third quarter was a momentum-changer for the Sooners, then came the ill-advised mistake in the final minute on a forced attempt to Cam Coleman in the face of pressure that led to Oklahoma's game-winning field goal.Longhorns' offense this season (SEC rank)Scoring offenseTotal offenseExplosive playsRushing offenseSacks allowedTFL allowed31.4 PPG (11th)379.2 YPG (12th)73 (15th)142.2 YPG (12th)12 (7th)35 (13th)Lack of execution is magnified after a loss and often get covered up following wins, but the cracks have been there for Texas throughout the season. Three points over the first three quarters of play during the win over Ohio State left much to be desired offensively, along with the 20-17 victory at Tennessee that was punctuated by 10 sacks from the Longhorns' front seven.Special teams errors aside, some of that could be absorbed if Sarkisian's offense was simply more productive. Texas missed the College Football Playoff in 2025 with an offense that ranked 70th nationally in production (388.5 YPG) and got there in 2024 despite being outside of the top-20 with Quinn Ewers at the helm.Since Sarkisian arrived ahead of the 2021 season, the Longhorns have only had a top-30 offense twice, the other coming in 2023. During that stretch, one could argue no coach nationally has had better talent at the quarterback position, either.Ewers rated as the No. 1 overall player in the 2021 class after signing with Ohio State before transferring to Texas. Manning shared the same distinction in the 2023 cycle and has entered each of his two seasons as the Longhorns' starter with Heisman-level buzz.Over three seasons in Sarkisian's offense at Texas, Ewers threw for 9,128 yards, 68 touchdowns and 24 interceptions, helping the program to a pair of CFP semifinal appearances. Execution struggles in both of those games stopped the Longhorns short of reaching the national championship.Manning's thrown for 5,254 yards, 45 touchdowns and 14 interceptions over the last 2.5 seasons, but hasn't always been sharp in big spots for the Longhorns. Against three Power Four opponents this fall, Manning has three touchdown passes and three interceptions and has been sacked 10 times.He hasn't yet returned to the confident passer we saw down the stretch of the 2025 campaign when he helped Texas win seven of its last eight games, including his performance during the Citrus Bowl victory over Michigan.Final story not yet written for LonghornsAt 4-1 overall and likely staying inside the top-five despite the loss to Oklahoma, all season-long goals are still up for grabs at Texas. The Longhorns host Florida, Ole Miss and Mississippi State over the next three games before going to Missouri on Nov. 7.The season concludes with LSU, Arkansas and Texas A&M over the final three weeks, all winnable matchups if the Longhorns can find some semblance of consistency and execution offensively.The seeding is different this week for Texas, but Sarkisian's team remains in great shape for a first-round home game in the CFP with a high-end finish. Ten wins guarantees an at-large both, especially with the resume-boosting victory over Ohio State last month.Another 9-3 campaign, however, complicates the conversation. And if it happens, Sarkisian will only have himself to blame.

title: Why is offense at historic low in the 2026 MLB playoffs? Plus more intriguing postseason trends - CBS Sports
description: We're halfway through the 2026 MLB playoffs, and runs have been incredibly tough to come by in October
body:
We're halfway through the 2026 MLB playoffs, and runs have been incredibly tough to come by in October
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:41 am ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Four teams remain, and something historic is guaranteed to happen this season. Either the Los Angeles Dodgers will become the first National League team to threepeat, or a long World Series drought will end. The Cleveland Guardians haven't won the World Series since 1948. The Milwaukee Brewers (existed since 1970) and Tampa Bay Rays (since 1998) have never won a title.    "This was a difficult year," Guardians manager Stephen Vogt said after his team's ALDS Game 5 win over the Chicago White Sox on Saturday. "For us to be one step away from the World Series, our ultimate goal, this is really exciting."    The Brewers and Dodgers will open their NLCS matchup Sunday night at American Family Field. The Guardians and Rays start their ALCS at Tropicana Field on Monday. Here are our biggest questions for the Championship Series, and here now is a look at three trends we've seen to date in the postseason.    
        
            
                Biggest LCS questions in 2026 MLB playoffs: Will we see best versions of Jacob Misiorowski, Shohei Ohtani?
                
                    Dayn Perry                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
    Offense is down. Way down.    Two rounds into the postseason, teams are hitting .208/.291/.334 and averaging 3.46 runs per game. It was a .192/.284/.304 line and 3.06 runs per game during the Division Series. Offense is down about 25% compared to the regular season. Offense always comes down in the postseason, but it is way down this postseason. Much more than usual.    
Here are the runs per game numbers:    Runs per MLB game: Regular season vs. playoffs    Regular seasonPostseasonDifference2022 				 				 				 				4.28 				 				 				 				3.66 				 				 				 				-0.622023 				 				 				 				4.62 				 				 				 				4.10 				 				 				 				-0.522024 				 				 				 				4.39 				 				 				 				4.21 				 				 				 				-0.182025 				 				 				 				4.45 				 				 				 				4.01 				 				 				 				-0.442026 				 				 				 				4.48 				 				 				 				3.46 				 				 				 				-1.02Usually, you can chop about half-a-run off the league average from the regular season to the postseason. This year it's more than a full run with most postseason games having already been played (25 games have been played and at most 21 games remain). If 3.46 runs per game holds, it would be the lowest scoring postseason since the Division Series arrived for good in 1995.    LOWEST SCORING POSTSEASONS SINCE 1995    1. 2026: 3.46 runs per game    2. 2012: 3.49 runs per game    3. 2013: 3.55 runs per game    4. 2001: 3.56 runs per game    5. 1998: 3.62 runs per game    There are a multitude of reasons for this year's drastic decline in offense. Part of it could be/probably is sample-size noise. At the end of the day, it is only 25 games. We're conditioned to think the postseason is more meaningful, and while the results certainly are as far as whether a team advances, it is still baseball, and 25 games spread across 12 days isn't that many.    The teams on the field are a factor, too. By runs per game, only six of the top 11 regular-season offenses reached the postseason. Meanwhile, 10 of the top 12 teams in runs allowed per game reached the postseason (that is, fewest runs allowed per game), and the top four and nine of the top 12 teams in defensive efficiency reach the postseason. It's a run prevention postseason field.Furthermore, some of the game's best hitters have been a non-factor. Aaron Judge is injured and did not take an at-bat for the New York Yankees. Shohei Ohtani is clearly compromised, physically. Jake Bauers, a top 10 hitter by OPS+ this year, is playing hurt, as was Ronald Acuña Jr. On the other side, the top five and nine of the top 11 pitchers in WAR have pitched this postseason.    Then you have endless pitching matchups that constantly put hitters at a disadvantage. Look at the average fastball velocity in the postseason compared to the regular season. This is almost unfair:    Average MLB fastball velocity: Regular season vs. playoffs    Regular seasonPostseasonChange2022 				 				 				 				93.7 mph 				 				 				 				95.3 mph 				 				 				 				+1.6 mph 				 				 				 				2023 				 				 				 				93.9 mph 				 				 				 				94.8 mph 				 				 				 				+0.9 mph 				 				 				 				2024 				 				 				 				94.0 mph 				 				 				 				95.0 mph 				 				 				 				+1.0 mph 				 				 				 				2025 				 				 				 				94.3 mph 				 				 				 				95.8 mph 				 				 				 				+1.5 mph 				 				 				 				2026 				 				 				 				94.6 mph 				 				 				 				96.1 mph 				 				 				 				+1.5 mph 				 				 				 				The average fastball -- average -- is 96.1 mph this postseason. Through 25 games, there have been more 100 mph pitches thrown this postseason (254) than the entire 2008 regular season (211). I can not stress this enough: It has never been harder to hit than it is right now. Pitchers throw so hard and have such nasty stuff, and they all get ideal matchups. It's an unfair fight.    Twenty-five postseason games equals 50 offenses and 42 of the 50 have been held to five runs or fewer, and only five times has a team scored more than seven runs. No team has scored 10 runs in a game yet this postseason. This is just postseason baseball now. Offense goes down every October, and this year it is down more than it has ever been in the Wild Card era.        Home runs are not leading the way    For several years now, home runs have led the way in the postseason. Runs per game go down in the postseason, you can scroll up a few tables to see that, but home runs per game go up. Homers take on added importance in October, and we've seen that this year. José Ramírez's two-run shot in a 2-0 win in Game 5, the Rays won a 1-0 game on a solo homer in the ALDS, etc.    Overall though, home runs are down this postseason, both in terms of homers per game and the percentage of runs scored on home runs. Here are the numbers:    MLB run/HR percentage: Regular season vs. playoffs    Reg. season HR/9Post. HR/GReg. season runs on HRPost. run on HR2022 				 				 				 				1.07 				 				 				 				1.16 				 				 				 				39.9% 				 				 				 				47.1% 				 				 				 				2023 				 				 				 				1.21 				 				 				 				1.34 				 				 				 				41.1% 				 				 				 				49.1% 				 				 				 				2024 				 				 				 				1.12 				 				 				 				1.14 				 				 				 				40.8% 				 				 				 				47.0% 				 				 				 				2025 				 				 				 				1.16 				 				 				 				1.20 				 				 				 				41.1% 				 				 				 				45.4% 				 				 				 				2026 				 				 				 				1.15 				 				 				 				0.96 				 				 				 				40.5% 				 				 				 				41.0% 				 				 				 				For all intents and purposes, the same percentage of runs are being scored on homers this postseason as in the regular season. The difference between 40.5% and 41.0% is nothing. The difference was much larger from 2022-25. Home runs per game are down, though. The difference between 1.15 and 0.96 is one homer every five games or so. That's significant.    This is unlikely to change the rest of the postseason. The Dodgers finished seventh in homers during the regular season. The Rays were 22nd, the Guardians were 27th, and the Brewers were 29th. The ALCS matchup guarantees that a team in the bottom 10 in homers will reach the World Series for only the second time in the last 10 years, joining the 2023 Arizona Diamondbacks.    One year is not enough to call the decline in home run reliance in the postseason a trend. It could be a one-off. It is happening, though. The "ball go far, team go far" ethos has held true for years now. It still does! The home runs just aren't being hit as often. This also contributes to the low-scoring postseason. Teams aren't putting points on the board with one swing regularly.         Positionless pitchers    There is positionless basketball in the NBA and positionless hockey in the NHL, where players are assigned a "position" but are free to roam around by design. Positionless play is coming to MLB in that the lines between starter and reliever have never been more blurred. Openers and bullpen games are the norm and a viable strategy now, not a last resort.    Through 25 postseason games, relievers have thrown 232 ⅔ innings compared to 207 innings for starters. That's 52.9% of innings going to guys who come out of the bullpen, and that is not out of the ordinary. Starters have not thrown more innings than relievers in the postseason since 2023. Here are the percentage of innings thrown by relievers the last few years:    Percentage of IP by relievers: Regular season vs. playoffs    Regular seasonPostseasonDifference2022 				 				 				 				41.3% 				 				 				 				45.3% 				 				 				 				+4.0%2023 				 				 				 				42.0% 				 				 				 				48.1% 				 				 				 				+6.1%2024 				 				 				 				41.2% 				 				 				 				51.9% 				 				 				 				+10.7%2025 				 				 				 				41.5% 				 				 				 				50.7% 				 				 				 				+9.2%2026 				 				 				 				43.1% 				 				 				 				52.9% 				 				 				 				+9.8%Reliever usage always increases in the postseason, and this is attributable to two things. One, teams are growing more comfortable with openers and bullpen games in general. They really did used to be a last resort at one point. The manager would get peppered with questions before and after each game about it. Now they're commonplace. They're just a thing teams do.    And two, the postseason schedule. The next off-day is never too far away. There were three off-days in the ALDS this year. Three in a best-of-five! When you know that rest day is coming, you can lean more heavily on your bullpen. The unforgiving regular season schedule rarely allows for that. Teams routinely go two weeks between off-days during the regular season.    The Guardians vs. White Sox series featured 53 pitching changes in five games. That just isn't something you can do in June or July or August. Teams are using the off-day-laden postseason schedule to their advantage, and that's exactly what they should do. Adapt to the schedule and adapt to your personnel, and more often than not, that means going to the bullpen.    
It's fair to ask whether this is a good thing for viewers and the overall watchability of the sport. I fully understand and appreciate the opener/bullpen game strategy, but they can turn games into a slog. The game has a hard time settling into a rhythm when there's a mid-inning pitching change and a commercial break every other half-inning, you know?    The four teams still standing all have at least two starting pitchers they trust implicitly. Also, we're now into the best-of-seven round, and Games 3-5 will be played on three consecutive days. That doesn't allow for the same bullpen heavy approach as the Wild Card Series and Division Series. We should see starters carry a larger workload moving forward.    There is no unringing the bell, though. Positionless pitchers -- maybe it's better to call them role-less pitchers? -- are here to stay and they have never been more prevalent than this postseason. The optimized matchups and the fact hitters rarely get those juicy second and third looks at a pitcher contribute to the low-scoring environment in October.

        The Missouri State High School Activities Association has suspended one of its football officials for putting his hands on a player after a touchdown celebration during Thursday night's matchup between Glendale and Kickapoo.Glendale wide receiver Joelle Rover began celebrating a 43-yard touchdown reception before referee Kevin Elmer grabbed him by the jersey in the end zone and put an end to his dance.Elmer can be seen putting his hands on the player, redirecting him and appears to be yelling at the wide receiver in the video."I think it really tarnished the whole game with that," Glendale coach Frank Tristan, said via the Springfield News-Leader.
In the video taken from the sideline, Tristan can be heard yelling "he doesn't need to be touching my player, you talk to me, that's ridiculous, you need to grow up" at the officiating crew working the game.
According to reports of the game, Glendale had received two unsportsmanlike conduct penalties earlier in the contest, which was won by Glendale 35-6;
Rover, a 6-foot-3 senior, has offers from Princeton, Western Illinois and Lindenwood, according to 247Sports. He finished last season with 11 touchdown receptions and 1,017 yards.

title: Biggest LCS questions in 2026 MLB playoffs: Will we see best versions of Jacob Misiorowski, Shohei Ohtani? - CBS Sports
description: The 2026 Major League Baseball postseason is down to four teams – the Tampa Bay Rays and the Cleveland Guardians in the American League
body:
The 2026 Major League Baseball postseason is down to four teams – the Tampa Bay Rays and the Cleveland Guardians in the American League and the Milwaukee Brewers and the Los Angeles Dodgers in the senior circuit. This means both best-of-seven League Championship Series are in the offing. The battle for the pennants gets underway Sunday night with the clash-of-titans NLCS, and then ALCS joins the fun starting Monday. To set the scene for these two series that will determine the World Series matchup, we've landed one crucial question for each of the four teams – the answers to which will go a long way toward determining the outcome of each LCS. Let's explore those questions right now. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Brewers: Will peak Jacob Misiorowski show up?Milwaukee's 24-year-old phenom is the hardest-throwing starting pitcher the game has ever seen, and he's also the heavy frontrunner for NL Cy Young honors this season. As such, he's essential to the Brewers' cause as they try to take down the back-to-back World Series champs. 
The expectation is that he's going to do his part and then some to elevate the Brewers to the World Series for the first time since 1982. However, Misiorowski's personally unprecedented workload in 2026 does raise some concerns, at least insofar as the remainder of the postseason goes. 
Last season, Misiorowski – minors, majors, and playoffs combined – worked 141 ⅓ innings. In 2026, his regular-season and postseason innings tally is up to 178 ⅔. Of Misiorowski's 2,735 pitches this season, 1,167 have registered 100 mph or greater. That's more than twice as many triple-digit fastballs as Padres closer Mason Miller, who's in second place on that list. 
        
            
                Inside the fastest show in baseball: What it's like to watch Brewers sensation Jacob Misiorowski
                
                    Dayn Perry                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
To be sure, the Brewers have been responsible in their handling of Misiorowski. Of his 30 starts in the regular season, 26 came on extra rest (i.e., more than four days between starts). Just three times did he throw 100 pitches or more in a start, and his highest single-game pitch count was a quite reasonable 107. Is it worrying that Misiorowski allowed two runs in four innings against the Padres in Game 1 of the NLDS? Not really. Is it worrying in light of the fact that in September he posted his worst monthly K% and BB% of the season? Maybe. When you see that kind of year-over-year innings jump in a young starting pitcher who throws unfathomably hard, it's probably something to consider. So we are. 
Misiorowski will be Pat Murphy's starter in Game 1, which would line him up to start again in a Game 5 and, heck, maybe even see a critical relief appearance in a Game 7. As such, we'll soon find out how much fire the best pitcher in baseball still has in that right arm. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Dodgers: Is Shohei Ohtani healthy enough to deliver at the plate?Ohtani isn't himself right now, and he hasn't been for some time. No, that didn't stop the Dodgers from dispatching the Braves in four games in the NLDS, but the Brewers are a whole other level of problem. It's going to be tough to beat Milwaukee under any circumstances, but doing so while getting little from Ohtani will be even more of an onerous task. As the question above implies, it's likely a matter of health for the best baseball player in the world.  Ohtani hasn't pitched since July 3, when he was pulled from his start against the Padres because of left knee discomfort and soreness in his right biceps. The more pressing concern is how those injuries, especially his knee, are affecting him at the plate right now. 
Ohtani's knee inflammation landed him on the injured list in September, but he returned in time to play the final five games of the regular season. He went 5 for 21 in those games with only one extra-base hit, a double, and eight strikeouts against one walk. Taking the longer view, Ohtani in all of September batted just .200/.333/.233, and overall his OPS at the plate dropped from .953 in the first half of 2026 to .772 in the second half. He also saw a decline in underlying batted-ball authority from the first half to the second. He hasn't homered since Aug. 18 at Coors Field. Against the Braves in the NLDS, Ohtani slashed .154/.267/.154 with, as the line implies, no extra-base hits. All of this is to say, it's been a while since he's been himself at the plate. As the Dodgers' team leader in a host of offensive categories – OBP, SLG, home runs, total bases, and walks among them – he's essential to an attack that's aging in spots and battling inconsistency in others. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Rays: Can their lefty-heavy lineup handle the Guardians' lefty arms?Coming off a sweep of the Yankees and a 98-win regular season that earned them the top seed in the AL bracket, the Tampa Bay Rays are obviously heavy favorites against the Guardians in the ALCS. That said, the Rays have a particular offensive weakness that Cleveland may be well positioned to exploit. 
Overall, the Rays this season ranked a respectable 12th in MLB in runs scored and an even better eighth in OPS. Consider, though, how they fared against right-handed and left-handed pitchers during the 2026 regular season: SplitOPS (MLB rank)xwOBA (MLB rank)vs. RHPs.752 (4th).323 (7th)vs. LHPs.679 (25th).296 (28th)As for the possibly unfamiliar xwOBA, or Expected Weighted Runs Created, it evaluates a hitter's or an offense's "deserved" level of production based on quality and frequency of contact off the bat. As such, it's more useful for projecting future production than traditional output-based measures are. When it comes to OPS or xwOBA, the Rays' offense is entirely lacking against lefties. That stands to reason, as the Rays feature a number of core lefty bats like Jonathan Aranda, Chandler Simpson, Liam Hicks, and Victor Mesa Jr. Yes, tactically adept manager Kevin Cash platoons where he can, but the lefty-heavy nature of his hitters means they're still exposed to a significant degree. As noted, the Guardians are well-positioned to take advantage. It remains to be seen how Cleveland manager Stephen Vogt lines up his rotation for the ALCS, but he has the ability to confront the Rays with multiple lefties. Rookie left-hander Parker Messick has been the Guardians' best pitcher this season, and he should be lined up to start Game 2 and, if necessary, Game 6. Deadline acquisition Foster Griffin also throws portside, and he may make multiple starts -- or at least be the bulk guy following an opener -- in this series. Joey Cantillo has been working in long relief of late, but he's stretched out enough to make a start or be the volume arm following an opener. That would pose problems for the one-sided Rays attack. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Guardians: Do they have enough power?Power plays always and especially in October. That's been the rule for some time, and it's again the case in 2026. That brings us to this potential concern in Cleveland. Here are the Guardians' relevant ranks during the regular season: 27th in home runs in MLB27th in slugging percentage28th in total bases27th in at-bats/home run26th in average exit velocity29th in expected slugging percentageYou get the idea. That low expected slugging percentage (xSLG) is worth highlighting; xSLG is based on the kind of power numbers a hitter or offense merited based on exit velocity and launch angle off the bat. In Cleveland's case this season, their xSLG of .369 was even worse than the actual SLG, which itself is a paltry .380. xSLG better projects future performance than SLG does. Speaking of which, the Guardians slugged just .350 in their ALDS triumph over the White Sox. 
        
            
                Guardians advance to ALCS with Game 5 win over White Sox: José Ramírez, Gavin Williams lead series comeback
                
                    Mike Axisa                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Things might not be as grim as they appear if lineup fulcrum and franchise legend José Ramírez is back to hitting more like his vintage self. Ramírez's power took a dive in this, his age-33 campaign. It's possible decline is setting in, but it's also possible that his midseason wrist injury took a toll. Maybe the further he gets from that injury, the kind that can sap power, he's finding more and more thump. Indeed, Ramírez homered twice in the ALDS, but he didn't have much help, as that .350 SLG for the series suggests. Yes, Cleveland survived against the White Sox despite that (non-Ramírez) lack of power, but suffice it to say doing so against the Rays will be a much taller order.

body:
An already hostile trip to Anfield gets turned up another level as Enzo Maresca and his squad face the music from the Kop following the Premier League's guilty verdict
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:06 am ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Anfield can be one of the most menacing away environments in the Premier League for any team to come to, but this weekend the roof may blow off the stadium as Manchester City come to town. With City having been found to have breached Premier League financial rules by an independent commission, everyone around the league has weighed in with opinions about what should happen. City are appealing the decision. The breaches cover 2009-10 to 2017-18, a span in which Liverpool finished as Premier League runners-up in 2013-14.  That season, Brendan Rodgers' Liverpool were only two points behind Manuel Pellegrini's City, with both teams scoring a whopping 100-plus goals in league play. Anfield never forgets, and the atmosphere could echo 2018, when Liverpool faced Manchester City in the Champions League quarterfinals. Not only was the stadium a wall of red, but so was the approach to it, which Guardiola admitted had an impact on his players. Even if this were a normal match, an undefeated City side would face a hostile atmosphere with Liverpool looking to get back into the top four.How to watch Liverpool vs. Manchester City, oddsDate: Sunday, Oct. 11 | Time: 11:30 a.m. ETLocation: Anfield -- Liverpool, EnglandTV: NBC | Live stream: Fubo TV (Try for free)Odds: Liverpool +170; Draw +260; Manchester City +145Anfield also hasn't seen Premier League soccer in almost a month due to scheduling and a lengthy three-week combined international break. The last home game was a drab draw with Fulham, far enough in the past that fans are ready to see the Reds again, and more than ready to respond to the City decision.1. Can City withstand the pressure?Immense pressure is on Enzo Maresca and the City squad coming into the match to show that the off-field issues are kept there, and the City boss has already called on his away support in a club interview.  "We need to be all together. I said many times the reason why this organisation in the last 15 years was top was because from the owner, the CEO, the sporting director, the manager, players, fans, they are all on the same page. And this is fantastic," Maresca said.  He added that his squad will be ready, but that he needs the fans as well while reiterating that he's calm about the off-field issues. It's one thing to say that, but it's another to back it up while in a hostile atmosphere. Social media has been rife with people's thoughts about City, and while players can ignore that, they won't be able to ignore the fans cheering and jeering from the Kop for 90-plus minutes.  It's a time when the players can come together in support of the club, but with thoughts of what comes next in their heads, a slip-up here could easily become the first step of a spiral. It's hard to predict which way things will go, but that's exactly why it's such an immense match, especially with Champions League soccer around the corner, with Paris Saint-Germain coming to town on Wednesday. City can't ask for a much tougher return from the international break than what they're about to get. 
How will the Liverpool fans react?It will be relentless pressure from the moment City arrive in Liverpool until the moment that they leave. City were already a team that Premier League sides weren't fond of, as success can put a target on your back, but now that even the methods of said success are in question, everyone is out for blood. There may not be a worse place for City to go than Anfield. Even against Manchester United, the economic concerns for Manchester if City were kicked out of the Premier League would loom over the match. The Red Devils may not like their noisy neighbors, but when it comes to Manchester as a whole, things are better when both clubs are successful and competing for league honors.  There's no such buy-in at Liverpool, a club with deep working-class roots. Money being funneled in from the United Arab Emirates is the exact opposite of what the Anfield faithful stand for, which only adds to the animosity that will be at the stadium. How City respond will be critical, as losing here could start an internal spiral, and that's just what the Reds will hope for. Although with punishment looming, it's an open question as to whether City's wins and losses will even matter should massive point deductions, or even expulsion get handed down. Home fixtures at Anfield are already massive affairs, but with the fervor of soccer's return combined with the occasion, this one will be something for the ages. What does the traveling support do?Former City manager Pep Guardiola will be at the Etihad for the Champions League during the week to show his support for his old club and City's continued claim of innocence, but that doesn't mean that the traveling support to Anfield will be just as united. Maresca has asked the fans for their support, but will they be unanimous in that? It's common for fans to voice their displeasure with ownership, but it's also tough to gauge just where City fans are on the charges.  While many fans are maintaining City's innocence, just as current ownership is, public proclamations don't always mirror real life, and if City's away support isn't backing the team, this will be an even longer game than if the players can draw on their away support amid the sea of red that most certainly won't be in their corner. City's owners likely face the possible option of selling the club, depending on what penalties are issued and whether they lose the backing of their most loyal fans is likely to play a roll in that decision.
This is also a litmus test for what City can face on their return home, which could be a rocky one. So much that is not yet known will become clearer on Sunday.

A 90-yard touchdown return by Josh Cameron was wiped out at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium as Bryan Thomas Jr. and Jeremiah Trotter Jr. were both disqualified after a wild sequence

        The Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars couldn't get through the opening kickoff on Sunday without some controversy. On the first play of this international game, we saw a touchdown nullified by four penalties -- which included two ejections.Jaguars rookie Josh Cameron fielded the opening kickoff at his own 10-yard line, and then ran it 90 yards back for the first touchdown of the game! So we thought. There was some yellow laundry on the field that was going to take away Jacksonville's big play.
There was so much for the officiating crew to sort through on this one play that it took several minutes before head umpire Ron Torbert felt comfortable enough to turn on his mic and address all of those assembled in Tottenham Hotspur Stadium to explain what happened. 
Eventually, the Eagles were penalized for illegal formation on the kickoff, while the Jaguars were called for holding on the return. Then, Jaguars defensive end Bryan Thomas Jr. and Eagles linebacker Jeremiah Trotter Jr. were both called for unsportsmanlike conduct after a brief scuffle, and both players were ejected from Sunday's contest. 
What's a bit humorous is that this was not even the fastest ejection in the Trotter family. Back in 2005, Trotter's father, Jeremiah Trotter, was ejected before the season opener could even get underway. He and Atlanta Falcons cornerback Kevin Mathis got in a fight during pregame warmups and were both ejected.
The confusing and penalty-filled start to the game was an accurate depiction for our London friends how this NFL season has gone over in the states. Just last week, there were  271 total penalties called. That's the second-most penalties ever in a single week dating back to 1950. There were 963 penalties in the first 4 weeks of this season.

After accurately identifying three major upsets last week, we examine five more for Week 5

        No favorite appears to be safe these days in the NFL, as underdogs have come on strong over the first month of the regular season. In the past two weeks, a total of 23 games have been decided by one score, which is tied for the most in a two-week span in NFL history. Naturally, those coin-flip games have produced quite a bit of upsets, and we've largely been on the scent with them. In last week's upset alert, we accurately identified the Texans, Lions, and Saints as favorites ripe to fall short, with the Cowboys, Panthers, and Falcons each pulling off upsets. Now, we turn our focus to Week 5, where there are several home underdogs, which always put our antenna up. Three of which you can find below, as they could stun the road favorites this weekend, along with two AFC East favorites possibly on shaky ground at home. All NFL odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook.Las Vegas Raiders (+3.5) at New England PatriotsWhen: 1 p.m. ET | Where: Gillette Stadium (Foxborough)TV: CBS | Stream: Paramount+Raiders ML odds: +160New England is coming off its biggest win of the season after going up to Buffalo and upsetting the Bills to get to 2-2 on the year. After it felt like the sky was falling in Foxborough, that win -- at least for the moment -- stabilized things. That said, this does feel like a possible letdown spot for the Patriots after such a monumental victory. They host a Raiders team that saw its undefeated 3-0 start get snapped by the Kansas City Chiefs last week, but Las Vegas largely hung in there. The defeat didn't expose them as fool's gold. Rather, I expect them to go into Gillette Stadium and make the Patriots sweat. 
Vegas ranks sixth in the NFL in pressure rate (42.5%) and fifth in sack rate (8.7%). Drake Maye was much improved against Buffalo's pressure last week, but he's still struggled overall when under duress and has had a propensity to turn the ball over. If that rears its head here, Kirk Cousins -- who is tied for the league lead in passing touchdowns (11) -- should be able to take advantage. Chicago Bears at Green Bay Packers (+3)When: 1 p.m. ET | Where: Lambeau Field (Green Bay)TV: Fox | Stream: (Fubo, try for free)Packers ML odds: +130I don't think it's hyperbole to call this a make-or-break game for Green Bay. A loss at home to Chicago would drop them to 2-3 on the season and, more importantly for tiebreaker situations, 0-2 in the NFC North. That's the makings of a hole that'll soon be too big to claw out of, no matter if Micah Parsons and/or Josh Jacobs return. So, with that in mind, I think the Packers -- who are admittedly flawed -- could throw the kitchen sink at a Bears team that is still dinged up. On top of Caleb Williams (hamstring) still being out and Tyson Bagent set to start at quarterback, Kyle Monangi (thumb) and D'Andre Swift (knee, hip) did not practice on Wednesday. They both could play in Week 5, but if they are limited in any way, that takes away/deminishes the identity of what this offense has been. Coming into Week 5, the Bears lead the NFL with 196.3 rushing yards per game. 
It's also worth noting that the Ben Johnson-led Bears have struggled against the NFC North. Against the division, Chicago is 2-5, while they are 12-2 against everyone else. Cleveland Browns (+2.5) at New York JetsWhen: 1 p.m. ET | Where: MetLife Stadium (East Rutherford)TV: CBS | Stream: Paramount+Browns ML odds: +110What if the Browns are just good? Cleveland is coming off a marquee win over the Steelers in Week 4, and will have the rest advantage over the Jets after playing last Thursday. After a season opener where it looked like the Browns were going to sink to the bottom of the league, they've ripped off three straight, and Deshaun Watson has looked solid. In fact, he's been clutch. Over this winning streak, he's orchestrated three game-winning drives and has completed 15-of-20 passes, averaged 6.9 yards per attempt, and has two passing touchdowns with no interceptions in those drives. Watson and the Browns now face a Jets team that has gone in the opposite direction from them. After winning its first game of the year, New York has lost three straight. As it relates to this matchup, it's the Jets defense that should be of central focus and possibly the reason for an upset. Sure, they got an interception last week, but the unit has struggled in the two games prior to Week 5. The Jets' defense ranks last in the NFL in yards per game allowed at 436.5. Watson also won't have to deal with a ton of pressure as New York ranks 28th in the NFL in pressure rate this season. 
New York is 0-12 in its last 12 games against above-.500 teams. Minnesota Vikings at New Orleans Saints (+1.5)When: 1 p.m. ET | Where: Caesars Superdome (New Orleans)TV: Fox | Stream: (Fubo, try for free)Saints ML odds: +105The Saints were embarrassed on Monday night in a 45-24 loss to their division rival, the Atlanta Falcons, at home in primetime. Typically, a team playing on a short week might be at a disadvantage, but I'd guess New Orleans is foaming at the mouth to get back out there to get rid of the sour taste of that defeat. Minnesota is 4-0 on the year, but that undefeated record has come despite some questionable play on offense. They've registered the third-fewest yards per game (262.8) during a 4-0 start to a season by any team since 1940. Meanwhile, Kyler Murray hasn't looked like the second coming of Sam Darnold by any stretch of the imagination to this point. Of the 28 quarterbacks who've thrown at least 70 pass attempts this year, Murray is 24th in passer rating, 25th in yards per attempt, and 27th in EPA per dropback. Really, it's been the play of the Vikings defense that has spearheaded this undefeated start. Brian Flores' unit has allowed the fewest points per game (12.8) in the NFL this season and has by far the highest blitz rate (71%) in the league. Against the blitz this season, Saints quarterback Tyler Shough has a 105.8 passer rating (11th among QBs) and five passing touchdowns (tied for third-most in the NFL), so he has been solid in the face of added pressure. 
If he can find some success against this Vikings blitz, that could be enough to pull out the win, especially if the Murray-led offense continues to struggle to get off the ground. Detroit Lions at Arizona Cardinals (+5.5)When: 4:25 p.m. ET | Where: State Farm Stadium (Glendale)TV: Fox | Stream: (Fubo, try for free)Cardinals ML odds: +210The Detroit Lions simply cannot be trusted as a road favorite with their current defense. They just let Bryce Young and the Carolina Panthers torch them for 32 points and 329 passing yards, despite it largely just being a two-man show between Young and wideout Tetairoa McMillan (14 catches, 192 yards, and two touchdowns). Detroit's secondary is giving up a league-worst 423.8 total yards per game, and their 31.8 points per game allowed is the second-worst in the NFL. Lions defense this seasonStatNFL RankPPG allowed31.831stYPG allowed423.8LastThird down percentage52.8%LastWhile the Cardinals won't be mistaken for a Super Bowl contender, they have enough playmakers on offense to take advantage of the Lions' poor defense. Jacoby Brissett is coming off his worst statistical game of the season, tossing three interceptions against the Giants, but he is capable of bouncing back and throwing it around the yard, especially with the likes of Trey McBride and Michael Wilson at his disposal.

Kirk Ferentz's squad is playing lights out defensively, only yielding 13 total points after the first three games of the season.Keep an eye on Iowa's rushing attack in this one. The Buckeyes' last Big Ten road loss in the regular season came in 2023 when Michigan clipped Ohio State, 30-24.Oct. 10: UCLA at OregonBob Chesney's coming-out partyUCLA is playing the primary disruptor in the Big Ten championship discussion early this season with one of the league's best running backs in Wayne Knight and a first-year coach intending to pull a Curt Cignetti and lead his team to the College Football Playoff. Another loss only amplifies the frustration, and neither program has much patience left for explanations under new regimes. This one is about finding a way to scrape out a victory.    Nov. 27: Nebraska at Iowa        A guaranteed Black Friday grinder     There's so much passion and history in this rivalry that was reignited by Nebraska's move to the Big Ten. Of the 15 meetings as Big Ten foes, 10 of the games have been decided by eight points or less and six have come down to a field goal.     Last season's 40-16 rout by Iowa was indicative of two teams that were finishing their campaigns in far different positions from a health perspective, as the Hawkeyes were wrapping up a successful top-25 season while the Cornhuskers were down to backup quarterbacks and barreling towards a 2-5 finish to the season. If both Nebraska and Iowa are playing for stakes late in the year, history suggests it'll be another close one for the corn rivals.
